title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Great investing is not about finding a company with zero risks; it is about sizing a proven compounder where the upside-to-invalidation math is overwhelmingly skewed in your favor.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Construction Maxim

web_blocks.html: Before issuing our final dual verdict, we steelman both sides of the aisle. The Bull Case: JPMorgan owns an unmatched U.S. deposit and payments moat, earns 20%+ ROTCE, and compounds TBVPS at 8.5%–10.5% annually [1]. It is taking share across CIB, affluent private banking (boosted by First Republic), and consumer cards [3, 7]. At 14.52x TTM P/E ($346.19) on a Stage 3 pullback toward support, re-rating toward 16.3x EPS / ~3.25x forward TBV yields $388.09–$425.00 [20, 21]. The Bear Case: A sharper labor downturn could push Card NCOs past 3.4%–4.0% [3]. Private credit defaults could trigger systemic counterparty stress [17]. Basel III Endgame rules could lock up capital, and post-Dimon succession could erode JPM's premium toward 2.6x TBV ($295.00) [14, 18].

web_blocks.html: Three-Horizon Independent Verdict: On the Short-Term Trading / Momentum (1–12 weeks) horizon, JPM sits in Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) at $346.19 with a flat-to-falling 50-day SMA ($340.42) during a market Correction [27]. Traders should wait for a pullback into $326.16–$335.05 rather than chasing below Pivot R1 ($346.84). On the Medium-Term Inflection (6–18 months) horizon, we assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2, CORE_ALPHA). Strong CIB advisory fees and AWM inflows ($7T client assets) support our $388.09 Base Target once support holds [3, 12]. On the Long-Term Compounding (3–5+ years) horizon, JPM remains a premier core compounder with 20% ROTCE and 8.5%–10.5% TBVPS growth [1, 20].

Current Holding Action & Capital Redeployment Plan: Per the November 13, 2026 US positions ledger, JPM is NOT currently held (holding_action: NOT_HELD, holding_shares_to_sell: 0) [27]. No existing shares are being trimmed or sold. For the next marginal unit of investable US cash ($3,818.88 available), we evaluate all three destinations [27]. We hold 100% in CASH until JPM pulls back into the $326.16–$335.05 support zone (4.23:1 R:R). We keep JPM (SHORTLIST) at 0% pending that support trigger (staged equity buys only, as the $4,933 LEAPS contract exceeds available cash). We allocate 0% to BAC (OUTSIDE) due to lower ROTCE [22].

Execution & Risk-Management Rules: Never chase a Stage 3 stock during a market Correction (6 distribution days). Stage entry orders in two equal equity tranches inside the support zone: 50% at $335.05 (30W SMA) and 50% at $326.16–$330.40 (Pivot S1 / 20D swing low). Risk no more than 1.0%–1.25% of portfolio net worth ($87,961.47 total US net worth, or ~$880–$1,100 max risk) [27]. At a $12.54/sh stop distance from $335.05 to $322.51, that equals ~70–88 shares.

What Would Change This Verdict: A weekly close below $322.51, an unexpected CET1 drop below 13.0%, or Card Services NCOs accelerating above 4.0% triggers an immediate downgrade to REJECTED; conversely, a high-volume Stage 2 reclaim above $346.84 with a rising 50-day SMA upgrades the setup.

Capital Redeployment Discipline: Testing every marginal dollar against JPM (SHORTLIST), BAC (OUTSIDE), and CASH enforces No-FOMO discipline [27]. Because JPM's Stage 3 CMP ($346.19) offers only 1.77:1 R:R, keeping 100% in CASH until $326.16–$335.05 protects capital while preserving readiness for a 4.23:1 support entry.

Final Underwriting Summary: JPMorgan Chase earns COMPOUNDER_PASS fundamentals and PASS KPIs, but its Stage 3 tape at $346.19 (14.52x TTM P/E, 3.22x FY25 TBV) requires patience [1, 3, 20, 27]. Waiting for the $326.16–$335.05 support zone with a $322.51 weekly stop lifts asymmetry from 1.77:1 to 4.23:1.

Monitoring Cadence: Once entered, review JPMorgan quarterly around earnings releases. Track three core gauges: Card Services NCOs versus the ~3.2% outlook, Standardized CET1 versus the 13.5%+ comfort band, and AWM net new asset inflows [3, 12]. Also watch CIB advisory pipelines and annual expense growth versus revenue. Keep the $322.51 weekly-close stop active in your trading plan at all times, and avoid averaging down below invalidation.

book_paragraphs: We have walked through twenty years of history, four business segments, a $100 revenue waterfall, ten years of audited balance sheets, a Reverse DCF, and a Stage 3 consolidation chart. Now you and I have to make a clean, unhedged decision.

Let us put the strongest possible Bear case on the table first. What goes wrong from here? First, if the U.S. economy slides into a genuine recession, unemployment rises, and credit card net charge-offs jump from 2.91% past 4%, JPMorgan's provisioning costs will surge. Second, if opaque private credit funds suffer a wave of defaults, JPMorgan's institutional counterparties could feel the tremor. Third, Basel III Endgame capital rules and Jamie Dimon's eventual retirement could compress JPMorgan's valuation multiple from 3.2x tangible book down toward 2.6x—putting the stock near $295.

Now weigh that against the Bull case and the math at $346.19. The market is already pricing JPMorgan for a fade toward ~17.5% ROTCE. Meanwhile, every segment is taking share: CIB earned $28 billion in 2025, AWM oversees $7 trillion in client assets, and Chase's 5,000 branches and 75 million digital users lock in the cheapest deposits in America. Even in our Base Case—where ROTCE eases to 18.5%–19.5% and TBVPS compounds toward $118–$120—JPMorgan is worth $388.09 (+12.10% upside plus a ~1.8% dividend). However, at $346.19 in Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) with a flat-to-falling 50-day moving average ($340.42), our invalidation stop at $322.51 risks $23.68 per share (-6.84%) against $41.90 of Base Case upside—just 1.77-to-1.

That is why discipline requires WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT rather than chasing at CMP. With a Compounder Pass on business quality but a Stage 3 tape during a market Correction, waiting for a pullback into the $326.16–$335.05 support zone lifts reward-to-risk to 4.23-to-1. Since our consolidated US portfolio holds zero shares of JPM (NOT_HELD), we hold 100% of our $3,818.88 marginal US cash in reserve until JPM tests $326.16–$335.05, and enforce a hard weekly-close stop at $322.51.

book_subsections.title: Position Sizing, Tranching & What Would Prove Us Wrong
paragraphs: Even when a business clears every fundamental hurdle, how you stage your entry matters just as much as picking the right ticker. Because the broader S&P 500 is digesting a Correction with six distribution days and JPM sits in Stage 3 below Pivot R1 ($346.84), we keep our cash dry until support is tested. Split your planned equity allocation into two halves: deploy the first half near the 30-week moving average ($335.05), and reserve the second half for Pivot S1 ($326.16–$330.40).

On an $87,961 consolidated US net worth, risking 1% of portfolio equity (~$880) across a $12.54 per-share stop distance ($335.05 minus $322.51) works out to roughly 70 shares—a meaningful core position that will never blow up your portfolio even if an unexpected macro shock hits. And keep three thesis-breakers taped to your monitor: a weekly close below $322.51, an unexpected CET1 drop below 13.0%, or Credit Card net charge-offs accelerating past 4.0%.

book_subsections.title: Why Holding Cash Until Support Beats Chasing Stage 3
paragraphs: Whenever you allocate a marginal dollar of capital, you face a three-way choice: deploy into your top shortlist idea (JPM), buy a cheaper outside peer (like Bank of America at 11.94x P/E), or hold cash. Comparing all three side by side makes the decision crystal clear. Bank of America looks optically cheaper on P/E and P/B, but it earns a structurally lower return on equity and lacks JPMorgan's #1 global investment bank and $7 trillion wealth platform.

Holding 100% of our $3,818.88 cash reserve makes complete sense when a leader is sitting in Stage 3 at 1.77:1 CMP reward-to-risk during a market Correction. If JPM pulls back into $326.16–$335.05, that exact same business suddenly offers 4.23-to-1 reward-to-risk. Patience is an active position.

Notice how freeing that mindset is: you do not have to guess whether tomorrow's S&P 500 session bounces or sells off. You have already defined the exact price zone ($326.16–$335.05) where risk-reward shifts decisively in your favor, and the exact price ($322.51) where you step aside if the market proves you wrong. Until price reaches your zone—or reclaims $346.84 on heavy institutional volume—cash is working for you by preserving optionality.

book_subsections.title: The Complete Checklist Before You Place the Order
paragraphs: Before you ever click buy on any stock—even a fortress like JPMorgan Chase—run through a four-point pre-flight check. First, confirm the business quality: JPM passed our blind audit with a 20% ROTCE and a 13.9% CET1 buffer. Second, check the valuation: at 14.52x trailing earnings ($346.19), you are not chasing euphoria; the market is already pricing in a fade toward 17.5% ROTCE. Third, verify the tape: JPM is in Stage 3 with a flat-to-falling 50-day moving average, so we wait for $326.16–$335.05. Fourth, write down your exit before you enter: a weekly close below $322.51 invalidates the setup.

Keep your eyes on the quarterly scoreboard as well: track Card Services net charge-offs against the ~3.2% outlook, monitor CET1 capital against risk-weighted asset growth, and watch whether Asset & Wealth Management continues to pull in net new client assets atop its $7 trillion base. As long as those structural pillars hold, JPMorgan Chase remains a premier core compounder.

And remember why this two-pass process works: we locked in our fundamental conviction on business quality before ever looking at the $346.19 quote, and then we let the Stage 3 tape dictate our entry price ($326.16–$335.05) rather than chasing below resistance. That separation of business underwriting from market timing is how you compound wealth steadily without getting whipsawed.

When JPMorgan Chase does test that $326.16–$335.05 support zone and holds above $322.51, you will step in knowing you own America's strongest universal bank at 4.23-to-1 reward-to-risk. Until then, keep your cash dry and let the market come to you, confident that patient discipline always beats short-term impulse in long-term compounding across every cycle.
